items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: First we had Budd Johnson on tenor, and then we switched over and got Rudy Williams.

ctx.x: Well, that was an interesting trip, which the Institute is very interested in. Of course, you and I have talked about this story before, but I think we should go into it in some detail. It was a USO tour.

Yeah. Well, Oscar had met this doctor from Orange, New Jersey or somewhere, and they had talked him into getting a six-piece group together so that we could play the USO camps -- which he did. We all got together. First we had Budd Johnson on tenor, and then we switched over and got Rudy Williams. It was a good band.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Howard McGhee was on the date too.

ctx.x: Piano player, who was -- I spoke of earlier, was the great arranger and everything. Clyde and I had been doing some writing together, and he says I want you to do something and I'm going to do some things. I want Dizzy to do something, you know,and we're going to make a record date. So okay, we made this record date and Hawkes, had Diz, Clyde Hart on piano, who else was on that date? I Played baritone sax. And any way I played on the date and I did this arrangement, Clyde Hart and myself (unintelligible) called…
